name: Fair Offer Standard
summary: Open rules for selling to AI agents honestly over x402. Free to adopt; no fee, no certification body.
how_to_declare: Put the fair-offer block in your 402's extensions (see handshake), and link this URL from your llms.txt or agent manifest as "conforms_to": {"fair_offer": "0.4"}.

versions.0.1: The seven rules, declared in an agent manifest or llms.txt.
versions.0.2: The same seven rules, plus the machine-readable fair-offer block in the x402 402 and the buyer's Accept-Proof header.
versions.0.3: Eight rules: FO-8, the same offer to every buyer, declared as one_offer in the block and asked for with Accept-Proof one_offer=checked; the pledge-ledger schema FO-7's ledgers can follow; and the platform annex, six rules for directories that list sellers. 0.2 blocks stay valid.
versions.0.4: Ten rules: FO-3's receipts bound to a hash of what was delivered (receipts.delivery_hash), FO-9, the price follows what was measured under the buyer's ceiling (metered, x402's upto), and FO-10, the book is open (book: the receipts ledger and buyers' reports); Accept-Proof receipts=bound, metered=ceiling, book=open and reports=open; and P-7 in the platform annex, marks earned by public check and never sold. 0.2 and 0.3 blocks stay valid.

rules.name: Price before payment
rules.rule: An unpaid call returns an x402 offer (HTTP 402) that states the price, asset, network and pay-to address. Nothing is charged before the buyer has signed that exact offer.

rules.name: Failure is free
rules.rule: A call that fails, times out or returns no result is not settled. The buyer is told so.

rules.name: Receipts are signed
rules.rule: Every paid result carries a receipt signed by the seller's key: what was bought, for how much, and when, and (0.4) the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 form of the result it came with, so a receipt is bound to what was delivered.

rules.name: Sample before you buy
rules.rule: A free sample shows what the paid route returns, and a third party can attest that the sample and the paid offer come from the same host.

rules.name: Honest listing
rules.rule: The listing's description, input schema and output example match what the route really returns. Edits made to win buyers must stay true.

rules.name: Data, never instructions
rules.rule: Responses carry data for the buying agent to use, never instructions aimed at it. A buyer can treat any instruction in a response as an attack.

rules.name: Promises are verifiable
rules.rule: Any claim about where revenue goes (a pledge, a split, a donation) comes with a public ledger that a buyer can check per receipt, with on-chain proof of what was given.

rules.name: Same offer to every buyer
rules.rule: Every buyer that asks at the same moment gets the same offer: the same price, asset, network and pay-to, whatever client, user agent or headers it sends. A price may change over time, never by who is asking.

rules.name: Price follows what was measured
rules.rule: A metered offer states its unit and one public unit price, the same at every size and for every buyer. The buyer signs a ceiling (x402's upto scheme), is charged only for what was delivered, never more than the ceiling, and nothing when nothing was delivered. The receipt names the charge and the ceiling.

rules.name: The book is open
rules.rule: The seller's receipts are in a public ledger that only grows, with a proof per receipt, so a buyer can match its own payments against it and anyone can check it. Buyers' reports, each tied to a payment on the chain, are listed and never edited or quietly removed.

platforms.summary: Rules for directories, indexes and marketplaces that list x402 sellers, so an agent searching one can trust the order it is shown. Free to adopt, like the rules above.

rules.name: No paid placement
rules.rule: No paid placement: rank can't be bought, and anything sponsored says so.

rules.name: A published rank rule
rules.rule: A published rank rule: the signals that order results are stated, and rank follows them.

rules.name: Sweeps aren't payers
rules.rule: Catalog sweeps aren't counted as payers.

rules.name: Removal with notice
rules.rule: A listing is removed only with notice and a reason.

rules.name: Extensions kept
rules.rule: A listing's x402 extensions, the Fair Offer block among them, are kept as sent.

rules.name: Fresh listings
rules.rule: Listings are kept fresh: a stale one is marked or dropped.

rules.name: Marks are earned, never sold
rules.rule: A badge, grade or mark shown beside a listing is computed from public checks by a published rule. It can't be bought, asked for or kept by paying.

pledge_ledger.for: FO-7: a ledger any buyer can check per receipt, with on-chain proof

handshake.stable: Keep the info identical in the unpaid 402 and on the paid retry: x402 clients echo it, and servers reject a payment whose echo drops or changes a field. Put live numbers behind a URL, never in the block.
handshake.urls: Each URL is https, or a path relative to the resource URL.

requirements.sample=any: the offer declares a free sample on its own host
requirements.sample=attested: the sample has an attestation on record
requirements.settlement=seller: failed calls are not charged (the seller's promise)
requirements.settlement=rail: the payment is captured only on success (auth-capture)
requirements.price<=listing: the live price was checked against the Bazaar listing
requirements.pledge=ledger: a pledge with a public ledger that answers
requirements.instructions=none: declared data-not-instructions, and no instruction-like text found
requirements.payers_30d>=N: at least N distinct payers in 30 days (Bazaar's count)
requirements.calls_30d>=N: at least N paid calls in 30 days (Bazaar's count)
requirements.deliveries_30d>=N: at least N deliveries in 30 days: receipts confirmed on chain, paid by buyers (evidence commons)
requirements.one_offer=checked: declared one_offer, and the offer read under two x402 client profiles seconds apart was the same, with no difference confirmed in 30 days (0.3)
requirements.receipts=bound: each receipt names the SHA-256 of the result it came with (0.4)
requirements.metered=ceiling: a metered offer that lists x402's upto, so the buyer signs a ceiling and pays for what was delivered (0.4)
requirements.book=open: the receipts ledger the block names answers (0.4)
requirements.reports=open: the block names where buyers' reports, each tied to a payment, are listed, and it answers (0.4)

accept_proof.answer: The 402 carries Proof-Match: met, or unmet; missing="...". A buyer may also add accept_proof to the block it echoes in its payment.
